title: Java essentials for web developers
intro: If you already know JavaScript or TypeScript, Java will feel familiar in many places, but its stricter type system and explicit structure require a different way of thinking. In this lesson, you will learn the Java essentials you need before building Spring Boot REST APIs.
takeaways: Java is statically typed and makes types and program structure explicit.
Classes, interfaces, records, collections and generics form the core of everyday Spring Boot code.
Streams provide Java's collection-processing style with operations such as filter and map.
Optional can represent a value that may not exist, while exceptions represent errors and exceptional situations.
Good Java code uses clear packages, encapsulation and naming conventions instead of putting everything into one class.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of a Java constructor?
options: To create and initialise an object
To make a class public
To convert Java code into TypeScript
To delete an object from memory
quiz.explanation: A constructor runs when an object is created with new and is commonly used to initialise its fields.

quiz.question: What does List<String> tell Java?
options: The list can only contain integers
The list can only contain String values
The list must contain exactly one String
The list cannot be modified
quiz.explanation: String is the generic type parameter, so the List is intended to contain String values.

quiz.question: Which Java type is specifically designed to represent a value that may be present or absent?
options: Map
Record
Optional
String
quiz.explanation: Optional<T> represents either a contained value or an empty result and is commonly used for potentially missing lookup results.

quiz.question: Which statement about checked exceptions is correct?
options: They can only be used inside records
They are always ignored by the compiler
They must be handled or declared by the method
They can never be caught with try/catch
quiz.explanation: A checked exception must be handled with try/catch or declared with throws in the method signature.

exercise.title: Build a typed shopping cart
exercise.task: Implement a small typed shopping cart. The cart should store quantities by SKU, reject non-positive quantities, allow removing a SKU, count all items, and calculate the total price from a product-price map rounded to two decimal places. If a SKU in the cart does not have a price, throw an error.
exercise.hint: Use a `Map<string, number>` to store the quantity for each SKU. When adding an item, validate the quantity first and then add it to the existing quantity. For the total, iterate over the stored SKUs, look up each price, and round the final sum to two decimal places.

tests.name: It adds quantities to the same SKU
It removes a SKU line
It rejects non-positive quantities
It calculates the rounded total
It rejects an unknown product price
